param.label: Analysis name
param.help: Used to name all outputs as {analysis name}_beegees_{output}. Letters, digits, hyphens and underscores only.

validator.message: Use only letters, digits, hyphens and underscores

param.name: samples_file
param.label: Samples CSV
param.help: Columns: ID, forward, [reverse], phylum, class, order, family, genus, species, [taxid]. forward/reverse are bare filenames matching files in the FASTQ collection below. The taxonomy columns are used as the expected taxonomy for taxonomic validation. A taxid column is required when gene-fetch uses the taxid input type.

param.label: FASTQ collection (all reads, flat list)
param.help: Upload all your FASTQ files as a flat list collection. The wrapper matches filenames from the samples CSV to files in this collection.

param.help: Obtain from your NCBI account settings.

param.name: input_type
param.label: Taxonomy input type in samples CSV
param.help: How gene-fetch looks up each sample on NCBI. 'taxid' needs a taxid column in the samples CSV, in addition to the taxonomy columns.

param.name: genbank
param.label: Download GenBank records for retrieved references

param.name: sequence_reference_file
param.label: Sequence references CSV
param.help: Columns: ID, protein_reference_path. protein_reference_path is a bare filename matching a file in the protein reference collection below. Every sample ID needs a row.

param.help: Upload the protein reference FASTA files as a flat list collection. The wrapper matches filenames from the references CSV to files in this collection.

param.label: R1 adapter sequence (PE; leave empty for Illumina default)

param.label: R2 adapter sequence (PE; leave empty for Illumina default)

param.name: reference_dir
param.label: Reference FASTA for filtering
param.help: Single FASTA file used as the reference directory source.

tool.help:
**BeeGees** recovers DNA barcodes from low-coverage genome skim data.
It wraps the following pipeline steps:
1. **fastp** — adapter trimming and QC (paired-end merge + concat, or single-end) 2. **gene-fetch** (optional) — downloads per-sample reference sequences from NCBI 3. **MitoGeneExtractor** — protein-guided barcode extraction across an r×s parameter sweep 4. **fasta_cleaner** — removes human contamination, AT outliers, statistical outliers, and optional custom-reference contaminants 5. **Structural validation** — HMM + reading-frame + stop-codon checks 6. **Taxonomic validation** — BLASTn against a local database with hierarchical taxonomic matching 7. **MultiQC** — aggregated QC report
**Samples CSV** (the file you upload)
.. warning::
Sample IDs must **not contain underscores**. Use hyphens instead (e.g. ``sample-001``).
Provide a CSV with the following exact column names. ``forward`` and ``reverse`` are bare filenames — the wrapper resolves them to absolute paths from the FASTQ collection. PE/SE mode is auto-detected: include ``reverse`` for paired-end, omit it for single-end. The taxonomy columns (``phylum`` to ``species``) are required and serve as the expected taxonomy for taxonomic validation.
*Paired-end example*:
.. csv-table:: :header: ID,forward,reverse,phylum,class,order,family,genus,species
sample-001,sample-001-R1.fastq.gz,sample-001-R2.fastq.gz,Arthropoda,Insecta,Coleoptera,Carabidae,Carabus,Carabus coriaceus sample-002,sample-002-R1.fastq.gz,sample-002-R2.fastq.gz,Arthropoda,Insecta,Lepidoptera,Nymphalidae,Vanessa,Vanessa atalanta sample-003,sample-003-R1.fastq.gz,sample-003-R2.fastq.gz,Arthropoda,Insecta,Diptera,Drosophilidae,Drosophila,Drosophila melanogaster
*gene-fetch with taxid input*: add a ``taxid`` column with the NCBI taxid of each sample. The taxonomy columns are still required for taxonomic validation. Any extra columns are passed through unchanged.
.. csv-table:: :header: ID,forward,reverse,phylum,class,order,family,genus,species,taxid
sample-003,sample-003-R1.fastq.gz,sample-003-R2.fastq.gz,Arthropoda,Insecta,Diptera,Drosophilidae,Drosophila,Drosophila melanogaster,7227
----
**BLAST database**
Select a database pre-installed by your Galaxy admin, or upload a FASTA file from your history (the pipeline will build the BLAST index automatically). The sequence IDs in the database must match those in the taxonomy TSV below.
See `docs/README_custom_blast_dbs.md <https://github.com/bge-barcoding/BeeGees/blob/main/docs/README_custom_blast_dbs.md>`_ for instructions on building a custom database.
**Taxonomy TSV** (``.tsv``, tab-separated)
Two formats are accepted — see the `custom BLAST DB docs <https://github.com/bge-barcoding/BeeGees/blob/main/docs/README_custom_blast_dbs.md#taxonomy-tsv-file-formats>`_ for full details.
*Format A — generic (``Feature ID`` + semicolon-delimited lineage)*::
Feature ID Taxon MH021436.1 k__Viridiplantae;p__Streptophyta;c__Magnoliopsida;o__Solanales;f__Solanaceae;g__Solanum;s__Solanum bukasovii
*Format B — BOLDistilled-style (one column per rank)*::
bin kingdom phylum class order family genus species MH021436.1 Viridiplantae Streptophyta Magnoliopsida Solanales Solanaceae Solanum Solanum bukasovii
The sequence ID in the taxonomy file must exactly match the hit ID returned by BLAST (``sseqid``).
